items.title: Palworld Devs on New Pals: Every Pal Added Should Have Something Players Will Remember It For
items.summary: Pocketpair explains to MP1st how they keep the Palworld roster fresh when adding new Pals.
items.content:
While Palworld was first seen as a copycat of Pokémon due to the catch-’em-all mechanic, the moment someone plays it, they’ll see right away that’s not the case.

Sure, Palworld does have creature collecting (called Pals) as one of its focuses, but the gameplay itself is more than that, as it combines collecting with survival, base building, and a more active combat system.

With over 280 Pals available in Palworld right now, and the devs adding more with every major update, how does Pocketpair keep the roster balanced, and what’s the thought process in adding new Pals?

This is the question we asked Pocketpair in our exclusive interview.

Speaking to MP1st, John “Bucky” Buckley, the studio’s Head of Publishing and Communications, answered our question on how the studio will keep the roster fresh as more Pals are added.

MP1st : How will you keep the Pal roster fresh and balanced as more and more are added?

Buckley started by saying, “We try not to think of new Pals as simply adding another number to the roster,” and not targeting a specific number when adding new Pals in an update.

“Rather than saying, ‘We need to release 100 new Pals with the next update,’ we try to add Pals in a meaningful way,” Buckley mentioned, and added, “Ideally, every Pal should have something that gives players a reason to remember it, whether that is its design, abilities, work suitability, combat role, personality, or sometimes just something strange or funny about it.”

Buckley acknowledged that as more Pals are added, it is harder to balance them for players: “Of course, balance becomes more complicated as the roster grows, so we continue to look at player data and feedback every time we release new Pals.”

I can’t say I disagree with Pocketpair’s decision. Thankfully, the game’s thriving, so the studio won’t be pressure to add new Pals just for the sake of keeping players engaged.

In the same chat, Pocketpair also told us that “maximizing revenue” isn’t what drives their creative decisions when it comes to Palworld spinoffs.

items.title: Palworld studio PocketPair won’t turn the game to live-service as “maximising revenue as quickly as possible isn’t what drives our creative decisions”
items.summary: Palworld developer PocketPair has revealed why it won't be twisting the crafting game into a live-service title.
items.content:
Games Blog About Us Careers Tutorials FAQs All News Features Guides Reviews Fortnite Marvel Rivals Arc Raiders Tutorials FAQs Palworld studio PocketPair won’t turn the game to live-service as “maximising revenue as quickly as possible isn’t what drives our creative decisions” Published:

PocketPair, the studio behind survival-crafting game Palworld , will not be pushing its games towards live-service.

Palworld has been immensely successful with one of the highest concurrent player counts in Steam history, but the studio doesn’t want to exploit its players with the trappings of live-service support. While the game will still see support, the game won’t be inundated with micro-transactions, battle passes, and more.

“I can certainly understand why some people might expect us to take Palworld in that direction,” PocketPair head of publishing John Buckley said in an interview with MP1ST . “But. For us, we just want to make fun games in our own way.”

Buckley added that it may seem “a bit cliché” to push hard against the trend of successful games, but that’s simply not what the studio wants to do. “While we obviously want our games to be successful, maximising revenue as quickly as possible isn’t what drives our creative decisions,” he added.

Alongside Palworld itself, PocketPair has pushed into spin-offs and even physical games such as the official trading card game. However, the studio isn’t looking to hyper-monetise its existing game to siphon more cash from existing players.

With that said, Buckley explained that the base Palworld experience isn’t going anywhere anytime soon. “The main Palworld game remains extremely important to us, and these spin-offs are not intended to replace it,” they added. “We see them as new ways for players to enjoy the world and characters of Palworld from different perspectives.”

In a follow-up discussion on Twitter , Buckley explained that the studio “could probably turn Palworld into a big live-service game with tons of DLC and MTX, but I don’t think it’s the right way forward for us.” They added: “We’re really not as financially motivated as perhaps many think we are.”

“I understand that the astronomical success of Palworld has blurred the public’s perception of what Pocketpair actually is, but we are, in fact, still 100% self-owned and more importantly, 100% self-funded,” they continued.

Palworld is one of the most successful indie games of all time, and the game is still poised for years of additional support. The game’s massive 1.0 update released back in July, with the 1.1 update currently in development at the studio.

items.title: With Palworld, Pocketpair doesn’t want to follow a Fortnite-style model
items.summary: Despite its immense critical and commercial success, Palworld isn’t spreading itself too thin and remains true to its original formula. Therefore, Pocketpair…
items.content:
Despite its immense critical and commercial success, Palworld isn’t spreading itself too thin and remains true to its original formula. Therefore, Pocketpair has chosen to release standalone games to expand this universe. One example of this is the farming simulator Palfarm .

In an interview with MP1st, John « Bucky » Buckley, the studio’s director of communications and publishing, discussed this approach. For him, copying the Fortnite model by simply adding extra game modes is out of the question. Pocketpair prefers to develop standalone games with different concepts.

« Well… I can certainly understand why some people might expect us to take Palworld in that direction (like Fortnite ), but for us… we just want to make fun games in our own way. I know it sounds a bit cliché, but while we obviously want our games to be successful, maximizing revenue as quickly as possible isn’t what drives our creative decisions.

When it comes to Palworld , we feel that some ideas would be better served as standalone games, where we can fully design the gameplay systems, pacing, and overall experience around that specific concept.

Palfarm is a good example. Rather than trying to fit that experience into Palworld as just one mode, we believe making it a standalone title gives it more room to develop its own identity and become something special in its own right. We don’t see this as one approach being better than the other. Different games and IPs will naturally benefit from different strategies.

For Palworld , this is simply the direction we felt made the most sense. The main Palworld game remains extremely important to us, and these spinoffs are not intended to replace it. We see them as new ways for players to enjoy the world and characters of Palworld from different perspectives. »

It’s worth noting that Pocketpair is also working on the dating simulator Pal♡world! ~More Than Just Pals .

items.title: Pocketpair shares stance on Palworld spin-off games and why a live-service format with tons of DLC “is not the right way forward for us”
items.summary: Pocketpair’s monster-taming survival title Palworld has been a sensation ever since its Early Access launch in 2024, and continues to enjoy popularity among gamers following its recent 1.0 launch. The company has since expanded its horizons, launching its own indie game publishing division called Pocketpair Publishing in January 2025, and Palworld’s own official TCG in August 2026. While the Palworld IP is also set to expand through spin-off games like Palworld: Palfarm and Pal♡world! ~More Than Just Pals~, the developers aren’t necessarily keen on continuing to expand Palworld itself in a live-service fashion. In a recent interview with MP1st, John “Bucky” Buckley, Pocketpair’s Head of Publishing and Communications, shared the […]
items.content:
Home News Pocketpair shares stance on Palworld spin-off games and why a live-service format with tons of DLC “is not the right way forward for us” Game Development , News 2026-10-14 19:08 Akira Sada 1 Pocketpair’s monster-taming survival title Palworld has been a sensation ever since its Early Access launch in 2024, and continues to enjoy popularity among gamers following its recent 1.0 launch. The company has since expanded its horizons, launching its own indie game publishing division called Pocketpair Publishing in January 2025, and Palworld’s own official TCG in August 2026. While the Palworld IP is also set to expand through spin-off games like Palworld: Palfarm and Pal♡world! ~More Than Just Pals~, the developers aren’t necessarily keen on continuing to expand Palworld itself in a live-service fashion.

In a recent interview with MP1st , John “Bucky” Buckley, Pocketpair’s Head of Publishing and Communications, shared the company’s stance on the matter.

When asked why Palworld hasn’t adopted a more metaverse-style format akin to Fortnite (like, for instance, integrating Palfarm into Palworld itself as a new mode), Bucky commented, “I can certainly understand why some people might expect us to take Palworld in that direction, but for us… we just want to make fun games in our own way. I know it sounds a bit cliché, but while we obviously want our games to be successful, maximizing revenue as quickly as possible isn’t what drives our creative decisions.” Over on X, Bucky added , “We could probably turn Palworld into a big live-service game with tons of DLC and MTX, but I don’t think it’s the right way forward for us.”

He presented Palworld: Palfarm as an example of this policy, stating that the team felt some ideas were best kept as standalone titles. Rather than making a farming side mode within Palworld, Pocketpair believes a dedicated farming game has more room to develop its own mechanics and concepts without being constrained by the needs of the main game.

Bucky also offered his own take on how the metaverse format has proven itself well for games such as Fortnite, saying that while he acknowledges that it works well for Epic Games, “We don’t see this as one approach being better than the other,” and concluded that different IPs will naturally adopt different strategies.

In his personal X post promoting the MP1st article, Bucky noted that Pocketpair is not as financially motivated as people may assume, adding that the company is 100% self-owned and self-funded, which means its decision-making process revolves largely around what the devs themselves find fun.

He also reiterated to MP1st that “The main Palworld game remains extremely important to us, and these spin-offs are not intended to replace it. We see them as new ways for players to enjoy the world and characters of Palworld from different perspectives.”

Palworld is out now for PC ( Steam /Microsoft Store/Mac App Store), PS5, and Xbox Series X/Xbox One. The game is also available via Game Pass for PC and Xbox. Two spin-off titles, Palworld: Palfarm and Pal♡world! ~More Than Just Pals~ have also been revealed, with release dates TBA.

items.title: This New Survival Game Finally Clicked with Me, and I'm Never Looking Back
items.summary: Palworld 1.0 does a great job of easing you into its many complex systems.
items.content:
Survival games have been wildly popular for years now. I’ve dabbled here and there to see what the fuss is about, but I’ve always fallen off after a few hours. Usually, I get tangled up in one meagerly explained system after another until I lose track of what I’m supposed to do, and my time with the game peters out.

When Palworld 1.0 came out to rave reviews , I figured I’d give the genre another shot – and I’m glad I did. Palworld’s gradual, newbie-friendly onboarding helped me see what a whole lot of people have loved about survival games all along. Palworld made me a believer.

I’m glad I came in at the 1.0 mark, because I’ve heard Palworld had a much steeper learning curve out of the gate. But now, new players start with a series of missions designed to guide you through the game’s numerous systems . You learn how to punch trees to get wood to create a crafting bench. You learn how to make a club you can use to beat some Pals to death (it’s a dog-eat-dog world out there) to get wool. You then use that wool to make clothes. You set up a camp. You build a house. You activate a teleporter and explore deeper into the game world.

Before long, you’re gliding off cliffs Zelda-style before whomping on every Pal you see to catch them in spheres to put them to work. You can deploy them at your camp, ride them , or have them fight by your side to take on big roaming Pals and towering bosses . It’s a blast. And there’s no way I would have stuck with it if it hadn’t held my hand and eased me into the systems that make up the game.

I still have a long way to go, because I was nowhere near powerful enough to defeat the first boss solo. But those early missions gave me a much-needed handle on what else I can spend my time doing as I level up enough to become a threat. There's a vast world out there I can keep exploring, all while catching Pals and building up my base. I’m having a blast doing it.

Palworld’s 1.0 is available on Steam , Xbox , and PS5 . It costs $29.99, but you can save a few bucks on a Steam copy at Fanatical , which is currently running its summer sale .

items.title: v1.0.2: Bug fixes
items.summary: \ Palworld version v1.0.2 has been released! This update includes improvements to gameplay stability and fixes for various issues. ＝＝＝ ▼Crashes and Disconnections ・Fixed an issue where all players could be disconnected during the Panthalus
items.content:
\

Palworld version v1.0.2 has been released!

This update includes improvements to gameplay stability and fixes for various issues.

＝＝＝

▼Crashes and Disconnections

・Fixed an issue where all players could be disconnected during the Panthalus battle on dedicated servers.

・Fixed an issue where players could crash during the Panthalus battle on dedicated servers.

・Fixed an issue where the game could crash when attempting Japanese text input in fullscreen mode.

▼Multiplayer

・Fixed an issue where, if a player was already in The World Tree area when the host transitioned to The World Tree area, the terrain could fail to display correctly from the host’s perspective.

・Fixed an issue where the Tower Boss “Victor & Shadowbeak” could disappear after using a teleportation attack during battle.

・Fixed an issue in the final boss battle where, if the host defeated the final boss while a guest was waiting to respawn, the guest’s light could fail to display correctly after respawning.

▼Missions

・Fixed an issue in the main mission “The First Islander” where the screen could remain faded out if dialogue was interrupted during a fade-out sequence.

・Fixed an issue in the sub-mission “Captured Adventurer” where the screen could remain faded out if dialogue was interrupted during a fade-out sequence.

▼Achievements

・Fixed an issue where the “Predator Hunter” achievement could fail to unlock even after meeting its requirements.

・Fixed an issue where the corresponding achievement could fail to unlock even after obtaining the required Pal Effigies.

・Fixed an issue on Xbox where the icons for two Lifmunk Effigy-related achievements were using outdated versions.

▼Graphics and Display

・Fixed an issue where the eye area of the player model could display incorrectly during cutscenes or certain player actions when using specific face types.

▼Controls

・Added key rebinding for "Attack that enemy!" and "Inventory".

・Fixed an issue where, when carrying over settings from versions earlier than v0.7, changes unrelated to Controls could still be treated as control setting conflicts.

・Fixed an issue where assigning a player action to the middle mouse button could incorrectly be treated as a conflict, preventing the setting from being applied.

・Fixed an issue where the Inventory Shortcut option was not displayed in Controls.

▼UI

・Fixed an issue where the damage number displayed when destroying ore while mining could sometimes appear as 0.

▼Performance Improvements

・Reduced the processing load during gameplay in Sunreach and improved performance.

＝＝＝

Thank you for your continued support of Palworld.
